the expression of genes involved in angiogenic and mitochondrial biogenesis pathways are regulated in response to endurance exercise in the Thoroughbred horse.

exercise-induced changes in gene expression in equine skeletal muscles are associated with genes that are known to be regulated by peroxisome proliferator- activated receptor-γ co-activator 1 α (PGC- 1α).

the gene expression of the PPARGC gene family is upregulated in skeletal muscle of horses after a single bout of exercise, and that this upregulation may contribute to performance in Thoroughbred racehorses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation.
the role of PGC- 1α as a master regulator of skeletal muscle metabolism in response to exercise.

the molecular mechanisms that control the skeletal muscle response during exercise in horses, which may lead to a greater understanding of exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation in humans and horses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented here provide a strong indication that PGC-α plays a key role in the regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation to endurance exercise in the Thoroughbred horse.

PGC- 1α plays a key role in skeletal muscle adaptation in response to exercise, acting as a master switch in the transcription of genes involved in angiogen-esis, mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative metabolism, insulin signalling, glucose metabolism, muscle fibre type and myogenesis.
PPARGC1B, FOXO1, MAPK14, MEF2A, SLC2A3, ALAS1, ANGP2, PDK4, PPP3CA and HDAC9 are novel exercise-responsive genes in Thoroughbred skeletal muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PPARGC family of genes play a key role in the skeletal muscle adaptation to endurance exercise in the Thoroughbred horse.

PPARGC1B and PPARGC1L are upregulated following a single bout exercise and are therefore potential candidates for further investigation in relation to exercise training and muscle adaptation in horses.

PGC- 1α and genes associated with PGC-1 regulation and function are involved in skeletal muscle response to endurance exercise in Thoroughbred racehorses and may be important factors in determining performance potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PGC- 1α and its associated coactivators play significant roles in skeletal muscle response to endurance exercise and may contribute to performance in Thoroughbred racehorses.

PGC-α is a key regulator of muscle function in horses and that exercise training may be an effective strategy to increase PGC-1a expression in equine skeletal muscles, which could lead to improvements in muscle performance.
